title: License details
summary: DJDL's product page opened at its License section (#/p/djdl/license) for Priya's Education license (the one licenses.detail shows), healthy, so no status pill: the License card leads the side column with the tier at its top right, the term on a timeline (a one-year license that keeps the last version), the facts, no key because the access policy issued it, and three add-ons with their source. Get it is one downloads table with this Mac's build tinted first; Devices carries a neutral meter (a limit, not an error); Cloud Sync, DJDL knows you as, What's new (Markdown, summary first) and Help complete the page. Each fact once. The phone render shows a phone's state: DJDL has no phone build, so the one solid action is Email me the download.
compare: Route #/p/djdl/license marks License in the in-page nav (from 1280 px) and in the jump bar (below 1280 px). One order everywhere: Get it, License, Devices, Cloud Sync, What's new, Help. Devices carries its count as the kit's neutral count after the label (ST-36).

Landing on a section route: the page opens scrolled so the License card's top sits just under the sticky header (under the jump bar below 1280 px), its outline flashes once for 1 s (no flash with reduced motion), and the mark holds on License until the person scrolls; after that it follows the reading line (PORTAL.md §4.20, owner polish 2026-10-07). Below 1280 px the marked pill is scrolled into view. The render shows the page from the top so the header can be checked.

Header (kit .product-hero with the portal's --hero-h): the back link 'Library', then the cover as a full-width band (220 px at desktop, 260 at wide, 160 at tablet, 112 on phone), the 56 px icon 20 px over its lower edge, the name (h1) and 'by Example Audio' beside it, clear of the art; Download for macOS (solid, the page's only solid button) and the ⋯ menu on the right. No status pill while the license is healthy (UI-KITS §1.5 rule 9: healthy is quiet).

Sizes (kit .product-layout inside the portal's content width): from 1280 px three columns, the 148 px nav | main (Get it, Cloud Sync, What's new, Help) | the 384 px license column (License, Devices, DJDL knows you as; 420 px at wide), which stays in view from 1100 px; under 1100 px one column under the sticky jump bar, in the jump bar's order: Get it, License, Devices, Cloud Sync, DJDL knows you as, What's new, Help. Every card titles at 20/28; columns and cards are 24 apart.

License card head: 'License' (the page already says DJDL) and the tier as a neutral pill ('Education', key glyph) at the top right, before any issue pill. No 'Licensed to' line (DJDL knows you as carries the email) and no device count (Devices says it).

Term block (kit .license-term, LX-41 through LX-15): 'Updates until Sep 14, 2027' over 'Then keeps working on the last version', the chart from Sep 14, 2026 to Sep 14, 2027 with 'Today, Oct 7' over its marker and a dashed 'Last version' stretch after the end, then the status 'You're on the latest version' (Get it's head carries 4.2.0). The track is --pk-border-strong against the sunken box, visible in both themes. No paragraph restating the title.

That wording appears only for keeps-the-last-version. A lifetime license shows 'Lifetime' and no chart; a renewing one 'Renews <date> · <source>'; a stop license at its end 'Ended <date>' with 'Renew with Example Audio' (portal.license-lapsed draws the keeps-the-last-version lapse).

Facts (.dl.cols): License source 'Automatic grant' (sentence case, P0-36), Works offline for '14 days', Release track 'Stable' (singular for one track), License key 'None, sign in instead' (an automatic license has no key, LX-38, so no key field is drawn); then the full-width Included: '4 decks · Recording · Cloud Sync' (the 1 GB is said once, in Cloud Sync's head). No Activated fact: the chart starts at that date.

Add-ons: a compact table under the facts, each add-on by its own name over its term, its source on the right: Polaris VPN · Lifetime · Automatic grant; Stem separation · Ends Dec 31, 2026 · From Example Audio; Extra devices (2) · Lifetime · From Example Audio (LX-15).

Devices: the head says '2 with Education, 2 from Extra devices' and carries '3 of 4 in use' with a four-segment meter, neutral (strong text at 80 %, never the accent or a warning: a full license is a limit, not an error); on a narrow card it drops under the title. One 56 px row per device: its 28 px tile, the name over one meta line whose facts never break inside themselves ('macOS · 4.2.0 · This device', the last in the accent; 'Windows · 4.1.3 · last seen Sep 30'), and Remove. The word is device, never seat.

Remove expands its row into the inline confirm panel (PORTAL.md §4.22; EXPERIENCE §7 L1/L2): 'Remove Gig laptop?', 'It's signed out of DJDL at once and 1 of 4 devices is free again.', on this device also 'You'll be signed out here too.', with Remove Gig laptop and Keep it, focus on the panel heading; then the toast 'Gig laptop removed' (not drawn).

Get it: the head 'Get it' with '4.2.0 · Oct 6, 2026' on the right, then one downloads table (Platform, SHA-256, Download), each file once. The build for this Mac is the tinted first row, 'macOS · Universal' over 'For your Mac · .dmg · 84 MB', with an outlined Download (the header keeps the one solid button); then Windows x64 and Arm64. Each file has a middle-truncated SHA-256 (mono, a hash) with a labelled Copy; the foot holds SHA256SUMS. No release-track picker: this license runs Stable only (P2-13's picker appears in the head only when a license grants more).

Cloud Sync: '37 MB of 1 GB used' with a neutral bar in the card head and no subtitle, then a compact table Synced data | Items | Size: Crates 1,240 31 MB; Cue points 18,920 tracks 6.2 MB; Settings 9 3 KB (tabular figures, never mono); then Export synced data and Delete synced data (danger outline). On a phone the two buttons are full width and stacked, Export first (UI-KITS rule 10).

Delete synced data opens a ConfirmDialog with step-up and typed confirmation (EXPERIENCE §7 L3): 'Delete DJDL's synced data?', the consequences (37 MB of crates, cue points and settings leave Cloud Sync; files already on your Macs and PCs stay there), Export synced data offered first, 'Type DJDL to delete', and the button 'Delete synced data' (not drawn).
DJDL knows you as: Priya's avatar, 'Priya Raman' over 'priya@example.edu · passkey', and 'Manage sign-in methods →'. It is the one place the account email shows on the page.

What's new in 4.2.0: the notes drawn from Markdown (kit .md: an h3 under the card's title, bold, italic, a list with dash markers, never disc bullets (UI-KITS rule 6), a link); the summary is the first list cut to three items, 'Show full notes' opens the rest in place; then Earlier versions as a compact table (4.1.3 Sep 22, 2026; 4.1.2 Sep 9, 2026). No subtitle: Get it carries 4.2.0's date.
Help: 'Help' with 'Example Audio handles DJDL's licenses and downloads.' and Contact Example Audio (outlined, external-link glyph) in its head; no body.

Phone renders stand for a phone user agent (PORTAL.md §5.4, decided by the device, not the width): the header action is 'Email me the download' (solid, full width) with the ⋯ beside it and the line 'We'll email priya@example.edu a link for your Mac or PC.' under them; the downloads table has no tinted row and no 'For your Mac', hides the SHA-256 column, and its Download buttons are icons with their labels; Priya's MacBook Air reads 'last seen today', not 'This device'. The footer sits above the bottom bar, whose Activate is the outlined pill.

Checks: no sideways scroll from 320 to 2560 px (at 320–360 px the table's Download buttons are icons); axe (WCAG 2.2 AA) 0 violations at 390, 1024, 1440 and 1920 in both themes; one visible h1; the screen writes no margin, padding or gap (its style block holds only the one-column order and the phone's untinted row).

designReview.reviewer: UX designer (visual critique of rendered screenshots)
designReview.verdict: Needs fixes, now applied: the light-theme duration track is drawn (3.2:1), the page has one solid button, and the phone state is designed; the scroll-following nav stays (owner polish) with the landing state specified.

findings.issue: Light theme: the duration bar's track was the box's own colour (rgb 235,238,248 on rgb 235,238,248).
findings.resolution: The duration box's track uses --pk-border-strong: sampled rgb(126,134,153) on rgb(235,238,248) in light (3.2:1) and rgb(97,105,123) on rgb(2,4,8) in dark (3.7:1). Same rule on portal.license-lapsed. licenses.detail is another area's screen and is not changed here.

findings.issue: Phone state not designed: 'Download for macOS', 'Recommended for your Mac' and a Mac marked 'this device' on a phone.
findings.resolution: Phone render: header 'Email me the download' (solid, full width); the recommended card becomes the callout 'DJDL runs on macOS and Windows · We'll email priya@example.edu a link that opens on your Mac or PC.', then All platforms; Priya's MacBook Air reads 'last seen today', not 'this device'. Compare line added.

findings.issue: Two solid violet Download buttons in the first screen.
findings.resolution: The recommended row's Download is outlined; the header's is the page's only solid button. The compare line says the real portal's recommended panel follows the same rule.

findings.issue: Route lands at the top of the page; the nav zigzags between columns and a scroll-spy can't mark one of two side-by-side sections.
findings.resolution: Partly declined: the nav keeps following the reading line and the side column starts beside Get it, because PORTAL.md §4.20's owner polish (2026-10-07) decides both. Applied: a compare line says a section route lands with the card's top under the sticky header, flashes its outline for 1 s (none with reduced motion) and holds the mark until the person scrolls; the render stays the top of the page so the header can be reviewed.

findings.issue: Devices subtitle broke at 'add- / on' and switched from 'devices' to 'seats'.
findings.resolution: '3 of 4 devices in use · 2 come with Education and 2 with the Extra devices add‑on' with a non-breaking hyphen; footnote 'Removing a device makes room for another at once and signs it out of DJDL.' No 'seat' is left in the copy or the compare list.

findings.issue: At 360 px 'Export synced data' and 'Delete synced data' were clipped.
findings.resolution: Cloud Sync's footer wraps, and below 380 px the two buttons stack full width, Export first. Checked at 360 and 390 px: no clipped text and no sideways scroll. Same on portal.license-lapsed.

findings.issue: Phone pill tabs used overflow: hidden, so What's new and Help could not be reached.
findings.resolution: The strip scrolls sideways (overflow-x auto, no scrollbar, scroll-snap x proximity) with a 40 px faded right edge; the compare list says the marked pill scrolls into view on load. Same on portal.license-lapsed.

findings.issue: Remove and Delete synced data had no confirmation or result specified.
findings.resolution: Compare lines added in the house patterns: Remove expands the row into the inline confirm panel (PORTAL.md §4.22; EXPERIENCE §7 keeps row-scoped confirms inline in the portal rather than a dialog) naming the device and the freed device, with the extra line on this device and the toast 'Gig laptop removed'; Delete synced data is an L3 ConfirmDialog with step-up and 'Type DJDL to delete', naming 37 MB and offering Export first.

findings.issue: 'Release tracks: Stable' for one value; 'Crates · 1,240 crates' and 'Settings · 9 settings' repeat the noun.
findings.resolution: 'Release track: Stable' (plural only for several); 'Crates · 1,240', 'Cue points · 18,920 tracks', 'Settings · 9'.
